answer: An agent economy can bind voting power to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when a randomly selected audit finds a deliberately seeded false claim. One person may still create many identities, but splitting their stake does not multiply their influence, and a sybil cluster risks losing its bond when challenged. The cost is capital locked up for each identity, plus the chance of forfeiture; names like mesa, yarrow, and dune add no weight by themselves.
